name: Understand AI

built.name: 1. Start with the unit: the Token
built.detail: Everything a model reads and writes is counted in tokens, and so is everything it costs. Until this one is clear, no pricing page on this site or anywhere else will make sense.

built.name: 2. What the model is made of: Transformer, Foundation Model
built.detail: The architecture underneath almost every current system, and the word for a large general model that others are built on top of.

built.name: 3. How it represents meaning: Embedding
built.detail: How text becomes numbers a machine can compare. This is the idea that makes search, retrieval and recommendation work.

built.name: 4. How much it can hold at once: Context Window
built.detail: The working memory of a model, and the constraint behind most disappointing results. A model has not read your whole document unless the document fits.

built.name: 5. Running it: Inference
built.detail: Training is building the model. Inference is using it. Almost every cost a business actually pays is here, not in training.

built.name: 6. Making it yours: Fine-tuning, Prompt Engineering
built.detail: The two ways to change a model's behaviour without building one. Knowing which problem calls for which is most of the practical skill.

built.name: 7. Giving it your facts: Retrieval
built.detail: Feeding a model your own documents at the moment of the question, rather than retraining it. This is how most enterprise deployments actually work.

built.name: 8. Letting it act: Agent
built.detail: A model that takes actions rather than only answering. Every governance and security question on this site gets harder at this step.

built.name: 9. Where it goes wrong: Hallucination
built.detail: Confident output that is not true. Understanding why this happens, rather than treating it as a bug to be patched, is the difference between a working deployment and a liability.

title: Understand AI: a path through the glossary, in the order the ideas build
answer: The glossary on this site is alphabetical, which is right for looking a term up and wrong for learning the field. This page puts the terms in the order the ideas actually build on each other: what a model is made of, how it is trained, what it costs to run, how it is made useful, and where it goes wrong. Every step links to the full definition. Read top to bottom once and the rest of the site stops needing translation.

points.name: Why this order and not the alphabet
points.detail: A glossary answers a question you already know to ask. A path is for someone who does not yet know what to ask. The sequence here follows dependency: tokens before cost, context before disappointment, inference before budgeting, agents before governance.

points.name: Where to go next
points.detail: Once these nine are clear, three sections stop needing translation: the model catalogue, the compute and pricing pages, and the compliance material, because nearly every obligation in AI law is written about one of the steps above.
